question: Does a forward torso-slide mode with friction-diamond maximum dissipation admit entry body motion and sustained progress using original contacts and actuator bounds?

population.selection: Only original R10AP partial entry1 / semantic step513; later poses are counterfactual models and carry no native provenance.
population.coverage: R10AU found no torso progress in any feasible sticking subset. This tests a distinct sliding contact law across all original support subsets and propagates only the prospectively selected admitted mode.

algorithm.subsets: Enumerate masks0..127 in original seven-contact order. A subset without a torso point is explicitly ineligible. For every eligible subset all selected torso points slide and all selected nontorso points stick; all excluded points supply zero force.
algorithm.friction: Retain authored mu1.8 as a model assumption and the same inner diamond abs(fx)+abs(fz)<=mu*fy. Choose the horizontal coordinate axis with largest absolute original heading component, x wins ties, and its heading sign. In that signed dominant-velocity sector the exact maximum-dissipation diamond vertex has f_axis=-sign*mu*fy, f_other_tangent=0. Do not substitute the circular-cone opposite-direction rule for this diamond.
algorithm.load: Same generalized gravity balance and published impulse/dt torque bounds. Append the sliding-friction equalities before the R10AR two-phase LP. Positive certified phaseI slack denotes failure of the combined balance and mode equations. Retain every primal/dual certificate and feasible force allocation.
algorithm.motion_constraints: Selected torso point vertical displacement=0; selected other points xyz displacement=0. Every selected torso point must move in the chosen signed dominant horizontal sector. Retain all-original-marker non-descent,24 shape witnesses, original speed bounds and0.02-rad nonworsening joint headroom. Body yaw/lateral motion is not artificially fixed.
algorithm.objective: First maximize torso-origin progress along the original horizontal heading. Then within1e-10 m of the optimum minimize sum(abs(delta_i)/maximum_i) over all14 coordinates using an epigraph LP. No arbitrary movement of unconstrained limbs is intentionally selected.
algorithm.finite_check: Mixed contact projection at most10 Newton corrections, four nonzero sample fractions and11 dyadic scales as in R10AS. Require forward torso progress>1e-9*fraction, every selected torso signed dominant displacement between successive nodes>1e-12 m, and all geometry/sector residuals<=1e-9. Re-solve the sliding-force model at every admitted node. Check force dot segment displacement against the friction-diamond minimum within1e-9 J.
algorithm.global_guard: During propagation, selected sticking positions and selected sliding heights remain within1e-9 m of original entry references. Also compare original-marker descent and24 floor witnesses to original entry so tolerance cannot accumulate.
algorithm.selection: Choose the admitted entry subset with largest finite forward torso progress; lower mask breaks ties. This selects only a model mode. Reuse its admitted first step, then repeatedly solve that same mode; no subset retries or mode switching after selection.
algorithm.termination: First model refusal, all-foot-cap COM hull gap<=1e-6 m, or600 admitted model steps. Preserve every attempted step, rejected scale, certificate and rebase. Hull inclusion is geometric only.
algorithm.no_tuning: No altered friction, caps, thresholds, modes, rankings or interpretation after exposure.

checks: 17 inherited manufactured controls plus12 signed-sector, drive-threshold and opposite-drag controls before source evaluation.
Independently replay original source entry contacts; synthetic states are never authenticated as native observations.
Retain primal/dual certificates for mode-force and both motion objectives.
Rebase the measured-relative geometry using R10AT identity checks; never normalize away native constraint drift.
Cold-process exact reproduction of complete survey and any selected model path.

research_sources.use: Coulomb friction, maximum dissipation, polyhedral friction and the distinction between contact models and actual dynamics.

limitations: Quasistatic force/kinematic surrogate, not static rest during sliding or an inertial model. The original friction coefficient is assumed for sliding, not a calibrated native material law. Forces are consistent with secant slide direction at sampled segments, not a proof for continuous velocity along interpolation. No native command transport, contact acquisition, release/rolling, dynamic transition, physical controller, continuous collision or interbody clearance is established. Original sampling/callback staging and penetration persist.
